name: Corner house
note: One solid corner: the round end of a row.

name: Row front
note: Two solid corners side by side: a straight street front.

name: Inside corner
note: Three solid corners: where two rows meet.

name: Pinched pair
note: Two diagonal corners: two houses kissing across a lane.

name: Block interior
note: Four solid corners: inside a block, no facade.

name: Spired corner tower
note: Convex corners of the university grow spires (see the spire roof).

name: Wayside shrine
note: A shrine at the end of a lane, round a tree or stone.

name: Plinth
note: The ground floor band.

name: Tall plinth
note: A raised ground floor, Gothic base course.

name: Storey
note: A middle floor.

name: Storey with oriels
note: Bay windows hung off the facade.

name: Cornice
note: The top floor, closed with a cornice under the roof.

name: Eave band
note: The top floor under a deep pagoda eave.

name: Gothic spire
note: Spires grow only on convex corners (end), the way Townscaper grows towers.

name: Layered eave
note: Shinto/Buddhist stacked eaves over shrines

name: Retaining wall
note: Where a terrace drops to the ring road below.

name: Stair
note: Where an avenue crosses a terrace edge.

name: Sacred gate
note: Where an avenue enters the sanctum: a torii with Gothic tracery.

name: Bridge
note: Where an avenue crosses the canal.

name: Well
note: Where an avenue meets a ring road.

name: City wall
note: The outer ring wall.

name: City gate
note: Where an avenue leaves the city.

name: Stone lantern
note: Along the avenues on the sanctum and shrine terraces.
